summary: Belarus waives visas for citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway and Iceland among them — for stays of up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia) at any international road or rail crossing, under a regime that runs until December 31, 2026; CIS citizens and a list of bilateral partners enter visa-free, and a separate 30-day waiver covers 76 nationalities arriving and leaving through Minsk and five regional airports. The foreign ministry says ordinary-passport holders of 68 countries, including the US, can get a single-entry e-visa for up to 30 days online; others need a visa from a Belarusian embassy.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Belarus, and Canada says to avoid all travel. The FCDO says you face a significant risk of arrest if you have ever engaged in activity now considered illegal by the Belarusian authorities.

The UK Foreign Office says the land border with Ukraine is closed to British nationals and other land borders have restrictions, and that if you travel directly from or to Russia the visa-free arrangements do not apply and you must have a visa.

The UK Foreign Office says almost no major banks in Belarus accept foreign cards and suggests taking cash in US dollars or euros. It says to use government-licensed currency exchanges and have your passport with you: if you exchange money elsewhere, you could be fined or arrested.

The UK Foreign Office says accommodation providers must register foreign guests staying more than 10 days, that your hotel will normally arrange it, and that if you stay with someone you should check that they do. Belarus's State Border Committee says breaking the registration rules can bring a warning, a fine of 50 base values or deportation.
Canada's travel advice says photographing military installations, public buildings and monuments may result in a penalty; seek permission from local authorities first.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Belarus?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of 38 European countries — the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and the European microstates — enter visa-free for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia, and no more than 90 days in a calendar year) at any international road or rail crossing until December 31, 2026, and CIS citizens and a list of bilateral partners are visa-free too. 76 nationalities (Canada, Japan, Australia and more) get 30 days visa-free only when flying in and out through Minsk National Airport or five regional airports. The foreign ministry says ordinary-passport holders of 68 countries, including the US, can apply online for a single-entry e-visa of up to 30 days. Others need a visa from a Belarusian embassy.

faq.question: Can EU citizens still enter Belarus visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes. The foreign ministry says citizens of 38 European states may enter visa-free through all international road and rail crossings for up to 30 days (90 for Poland, Lithuania and Latvia) until December 31, 2026, with no more than 90 days of visa-free stay in a calendar year.

faq.question: Can I enter Belarus overland from Russia?
faq.answer: Only with a visa. The UK Foreign Office says that if you travel directly from or to Russia the visa-free arrangements do not apply and you must have a visa, and that since 11 January 2025 foreign citizens with a Belarusian or Russian visa may enter, leave, stay in or transit either country at certain international border crossings.

faq.question: Do foreign bank cards work in Belarus?
faq.answer: Often not. The UK Foreign Office says almost no major banks in Belarus accept foreign cards, those that do may charge a higher commission, and UK banks may block cards used in Belarus because of sanctions. It suggests taking US dollars or euros.

faq.question: Is travel insurance required for Belarus?
faq.answer: Yes. When crossing the border, foreign visitors must have a medical insurance document from a Belarusian or foreign insurer, except categories not obliged to hold one. Under the airport visa-free regime the policy must give at least EUR 10,000 of cover for the whole stay.

faq.question: Is it safe to visit Belarus?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Belarus and Canada says to avoid all travel. The FCDO cites a significant risk of arrest for anyone who has engaged in activity now considered illegal there, and a low risk that the war in Ukraine spreads to Belarus.
